residency.test: Unlimited liability if you have a domicile (a dwelling you can use) or habitual abode of more than six months in Austria.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for unlimited taxpayers, with treaty relief and progression.
residency.note: Austria applies the same Wohnsitz concept as Germany, so keeping an available home can create residence even with limited presence.

headline.social_security: about 18.12% employee up to a monthly ceiling
headline.13th_and_14th_salaries: the two extra monthly salaries are taxed at just 6% within limits

standard_deduction.name: Werbungskostenpauschale
standard_deduction.note: small flat allowance; most employees claim actual costs instead

credits.name: Familienbonus Plus
credits.note: 2,000 per child under 18, 700 after; split between parents

employee.name: Sozialversicherung (pension, health, unemployment, accident)
employee.note: monthly ceiling of 6,450 including the special payments

capital_gains.financial_assets: 27.5% flat rate (Kapitalertragsteuer) on dividends, interest from securities and capital gains
capital_gains.real_estate: 30% Immobilienertragsteuer, with a reduced effective rate for property acquired before 2002
capital_gains.principal_residence: exempt if it was your main residence for two years before sale, or five of the last ten

quirks: The 13th and 14th salaries (Urlaubsgeld and Weihnachtsgeld) are taxed at 6% within the annual sixth (Jahressechstel). This is a genuine structural advantage - annual take-home is materially higher than a naive monthly calculation suggests.

Most employees are not required to file, but the voluntary assessment (Arbeitnehmerveranlagung) can be filed for five prior years and usually produces a refund, particularly if you worked part of a year.
The Pendlerpauschale for commuting is generous where public transport is not reasonable, and is claimed through payroll or the annual return.
Austria has no wealth tax and no inheritance tax, which is unusual for a high-tax European country.
The Familienbonus Plus is a credit rather than an allowance, so it is worth the same to every parent regardless of marginal rate.

reporting.who_must_file: Mandatory for self-employed income above 730 where total income exceeds 12,816, for taxpayers with two or more simultaneous employments, and where certain credits were applied in payroll. Voluntary otherwise.

deadlines.what: Extended deadline when represented by a Steuerberater
Last date for a voluntary Arbeitnehmerveranlagung for 2025 (five years)

forms.name: Annual payroll statement filed by the employer

documents_to_collect: Jahreslohnzettel from each employer (usually already transmitted electronically)
Receipts for work equipment, professional training and travel
Church contribution, donation and private pension certificates

penalties.late_filing: Verspätungszuschlag of up to 10% of the assessed tax
penalties.late_payment: Säumniszuschlag of 2%, with further 1% charges after three and six months
penalties.interest: Anspruchszinsen from 1 October of the following year

warnings: The 6% rate on the 13th and 14th salaries is not applied. For employees paid 14 salaries, the real annual tax is lower than this model shows.
The single blended social security rate hides small differences between white-collar and blue-collar schemes.
Church tax (Kirchenbeitrag) is deductible up to 600 and is not modelled.
